name: NoMeansNo
label: Alternative Tentacles
lede: Two brothers in Victoria couldn't find a guitarist, so a bass and a drum kit did the job. Thirty-seven years later, in 2016, John Wright announced the retirement.

eras.title: A slogan off a wall, no guitarist in sight
eras.text: Two brothers in a Victoria basement build a band around a bass and a drum kit because nobody they know plays guitar. By 1984 they have three records, a guitarist and a hockey-themed Ramones cover band on the side.

years.h: Rob and John Wright start a band in their parents' basement
years.p: Rob is 25 and back from Calgary; his younger brother John drums in a school jazz band. They take the name from an anti-date-rape slogan on a graffitied wall.
years.xp:
Rob Wright plays guitar and bass, John Wright plays keyboards and drums, and both sing, all on a TASCAM four-track. For a while the brothers also work as the rhythm section of a local cover band called Castle.

What pushes John toward punk is a [[D.O.A.|0f0b2f97-a073-4a92-ab99-ff7980ad7fca]] show at the University of Victoria. He tells Big Takeover that the singles "13" and "The Prisoner" got him there, and the show made him want to see more.

years.h: Betrayal, Fear, Anger, Hatred is the first EP, self-released
years.p: It follows a 1980 split single with Mass Appeal. In 1981 the brothers also start playing live as a bass-and-drums duo.
years.xp: The 1980 split single pairs "Look, Here Come the Wormies" with Mass Appeal's "SS Social Service". With no guitarist, John Wright says later, "you can't rely on the standard hooks" of punk, so the bass and drums have to carry the writing.

years.h: The first album, Mama, gets a limited pressing
years.p: Self-released, bass and drums only. Trouser Press's Ira Robbins files it under "Devo on a jazz trip, Motörhead after art school, or Wire on psychotic steroids."
years.xp: Robbins's line is the one early NoMeansNo write-ups keep reaching for: a duo that sounds nothing like a punk band is supposed to. The brothers keep working around Victoria and BC while Mama circulates in small numbers.

yt: Rob Wright and Andy Kerr interview, March 1989
years.h: Andy Kerr arrives from the Infamous Scientists
years.p: He runs a Fender Bassman through a PA speaker, and the jagged, buzzing tone he gets defines the next nine years.
years.xp: Kerr comes from the Victoria punk band the Infamous Scientists, which split in 1982 after two EPs. He becomes the guitarist and a second singer, and when [[Rob Wright|dd8d4145-d3a0-4b33-b217-0dc424ca423e]] later has surgery for vocal nodules, Kerr takes most of the lead vocals for a stretch.

yt: John Wright on the Hanson Brothers, 2009
years.h: A hockey-gear Ramones cover band, on the side
years.p: The Hanson Brothers take their name from the goons in the film Slap Shot. They start as an occasional Ramones cover set, then begin writing their own Ramones songs.
years.xp: The Wrights and Kerr play as Canadian hockey players and fans, borrowing the look and the names from the 1977 film. Tom Holliston joins on guitar in 1989 and John moves to lead vocals; the band's album covers go on to parody the Ramones, Black Flag and D.O.A.

eras.title: Sex Mad reaches Jello Biafra
eras.text: With Andy Kerr in, the trio makes an EP on a Vancouver label and a full album in Montreal. Jello Biafra hears it, and Alternative Tentacles follows.

years.h: The trio's first record, You Kill Me, includes a Hendrix cover
years.p: Recorded at Mushroom Studios in Vancouver with Greg Reely: four originals and "Manic Depression".
years.xp: The EP comes out on Undergrowth Records. Alternative Tentacles reissues a remixed version in 1991, and it later ships bundled with Sex Mad. Trouser Press points to the EP's dark humor and musicianship.

years.h: Sex Mad goes from a Montreal label to Jello Biafra
years.p: Psyche Industry of Montreal puts it out. Alternative Tentacles later issues it in the US and Europe with a reworked track list.
years.xp: It is the first session with Craig Bougie, who becomes the band's live sound engineer for close to two decades. Canadian critics call it the band's finest work to date. AllMusic later lists it among the band's most accessible records.

years.cap: Flyer for D.O.A. with NoMeansNo, Pine Street Theatre, Portland, Oct 24, 1987
years.h: "Dad" backed with "Revenge" gets college radio play
years.p: The single off Sex Mad is NoMeansNo's first minor radio hit, and its calling card in the US.
years.xp: The band also tours seven weeks with [[D.O.A.|0f0b2f97-a073-4a92-ab99-ff7980ad7fca]] in 1987, John Wright tells The Quietus. He recalls an early US tour where they did not play a Friday or Saturday night for three months.

eras.title: Wrong, a Biafra record and a brawl in Milan
eras.text: The label deal, the record everyone names first, a collaboration with Biafra and a European circuit that pays the bills. Kerr's last album closes the run.

years.src: Wikipedia: Small Parts Isolated and Destroyed · PM Press
years.h: Small Parts Isolated and Destroyed opens the Alternative Tentacles years
years.p: Cut at Profile Sound in Vancouver in December 1987 with producer Cecil English. The same sessions yield the EP The Day Everything Became Nothing.
years.xp:
Alternative Tentacles later couples the two on one CD as The Day Everything Became Isolated and Destroyed. AllMusic's Sean Carruthers gives Small Parts 2.5 stars and finds it lacked zip.

Jello Biafra recalls the band's first San Francisco show for PM Press's oral history: "Playing to a tiny crowd at a tiny dive bar. Blew the roof off several buildings in a matter of minutes."

years.h: Squatters from Turin crash a Milan show before song three
years.p: John Wright says about fifty people were fighting around the band before they finished two songs. A second brawl stopped the show.
years.xp: John Wright tells The Quietus that communist squatters from Turin forced their way into the venue during setup. The band got through two songs before the second brawl ended it. The interview gives no year; 1989 is our estimate.

years.src: Wikipedia: Wrong (album) · Big Takeover · Alternative Tentacles
years.h: Wrong is recorded in summer and out by autumn
years.p: Recorded at Profile Sound in Vancouver and released on Alternative Tentacles. John Wright calls it "most popular album by a country mile".
years.xp:
The Collector's Guide to Heavy Metal gives it a 10 out of 10. AllMusic's Sean Carruthers calls it the band's masterpiece.

John Wright ties its reach to Europe, where their fanbase built, and to the alternative boom after Nirvana. He also says the band stopped needing day jobs in 1990.

years.cap: Jello Biafra with NoMeansNo, Alternative Tentacles
years.src: Wikipedia: The Sky Is Falling and I Want My Mommy
years.h: Jello Biafra takes the mic for The Sky Is Falling and I Want My Mommy
years.p: It grows out of one song for the film Terminal City Ricochet, and the title track is re-recorded with new words.
years.xp: Biafra co-produces with Mr. Right and Buttercup, the Wrights' production names. "Bruce's Diary" was written after the film, from the point of view of Biafra's movie character, and exists only on this record. Runtime is 35 minutes and 50 seconds.

years.h: 0 + 2 = 1 is Andy Kerr's last record as a full member
years.p: Recorded at Profile Sound in July: nineteen songs cut, eleven kept.
years.xp:
The eight left-behind songs turn up later on compilations and albums. AllMusic's Adam Bregman finds great moments on a record that is too long and gives it three stars. Alternative Tentacles issues it on CD, LP and cassette.

Hometown footage from the same month exists: a July 19, 1991 set at the Cedar Hill Rec Center in Victoria.

eras.title: Back to two, then four
eras.text: Kerr moves to Amsterdam and the brothers go back to a duo for Mr. Happy. Then Tom Holliston and a second drummer arrive, and the band slows down and stretches out for the rest of the decade.

years.cap: NoMeansNo live at the Spirit, circa 1992
years.h: Andy Kerr moves to Amsterdam and leaves the band
years.p: After the 0 + 2 = 1 tour he emigrates to the Netherlands. Sources put the exit in 1991 or 1992.
years.xp: In Amsterdam Kerr trades airmail cassettes with Scott Henderson to make two albums as Hissanol for Alternative Tentacles. He later forms Two Pin Din with Wilf Plum, formerly of the Dog Faced Hermans.

years.cap: The Hanson Brothers live at Bogarts
years.src: Wikipedia: The Hanson Brothers (band) · Wikipedia: Nomeansno
years.h: The Hanson Brothers get their own album, Gross Misconduct
years.p: Alternative Tentacles turns the Ramones-style side project into a record, with Ken Jensen of D.O.A. on drums.
years.xp: Around now Rob Wright also plays solo as Mr. Wrong in a priest character, and John Wright drums with D.O.A. for several years. Jensen dies in a house fire in 1995, according to Wikipedia; Ken Kempster takes the Hanson Brothers drum seat.

years.src: Wikipedia: Why Do They Call Me Mr. Happy?
years.h: The duo is back for Why Do They Call Me Mr. Happy?
years.p: It is a duo record for the first time since Mama. The last track builds in samples from Faith No More, the Residents and Deep Purple.
years.xp: Of the ten CD tracks, three predate Kerr's exit and four come from Rob Wright's Mr. Wrong project. AllMusic's Ned Raggett gives it 4.5 stars. Decades later the Guardian's John Doran calls it "the high watermark of western civilization".

years.cap: Flyer for NoMeansNo with Agent 86, WOW Hall, Eugene, Dec 6, 1993
years.h: Tom Holliston and Ken Kempster make it a four-piece
years.p: Holliston, from Showbusiness Giants, joins for the Mr. Happy tour. Kempster follows on second drums later in 1993.
years.xp: Kempster plays with the band only sporadically over the next four years. Holliston is the guitarist for the rest of NoMeansNo's run.

years.h: The Worldhood of the World (As Such) borrows a Heidegger title
years.p: It is the first record for the four-piece. Rob Wright tells the Spokesman-Review it "almost sounds like a punk rock album".
years.xp: The Spokesman-Review counts it as the ninth album for Alternative Tentacles and the eleventh overall. In the same interview Rob Wright says major labels charge a big price too.

years.h: Dance of the Headless Bourgeoisie is a double LP of the longest songs yet
years.p: Reviews split: AllMusic's Tom Schulte calls it dark and unforgettable, and The A.V. Club calls it "dull, meandering punk".

years.h: One is the last record for Alternative Tentacles
years.p: It includes a slow, heavy take on the Ramones' "Beat on the Brat" and a fifteen-minute version of Miles Davis's "Bitches Brew".
years.xp: Schulte calls it the band's best since Wrong. Three outtakes come out later as the Generic Shame EP on the band's own Wrong Records.

eras.title: On their own, until 2016
eras.text: Free of Alternative Tentacles, the brothers self-release, tour Europe hard and make one more album. In 2016 the hiatus becomes a retirement.

yt: Live at the Starfish Room, Vancouver, 2002
years.h: NoMeansNo walks away from Alternative Tentacles over European distribution
years.p: They reissue their back catalog on their own Wrong Records, distributed by Southern.
years.xp: Wikipedia gives European distribution as the main reason, since that is where the fans were. John Wright tells The Quietus that Jello Biafra is "very eccentric, very smart" and dates the end of the relationship to around 2003 or 2004. The band also regains its catalog rights in 2002.

years.h: All Roads Lead to Ausfahrt is the tenth and last studio album
years.p: Out on AntAcidAudio in the US and Southern in Europe. John Wright wrote most of the music.
years.xp: Rob Wright tells Alienated in Vancouver that he wrote lyrics for eleven songs about a month before recording. He describes "Slugs Are Burning" as one that took him a year and a half to understand.

years.cap: NoMeansNo at the Kleiner Klub, Saarbruecken
years.h: John Wright counts 172 shows between late 2006 and 2007
years.p: He tells Vice that was the most money he ever made in a year from the band.
years.xp: The band tours about three months a year by that point. John Wright says the band stopped needing day jobs in 1990, while Rob "still is" a dishwasher and volunteers at a soup kitchen.

years.cap: Rob Wright at Tivoli de Helling, Utrecht
q: If you just last long enough, people start to notice
years.h: NoMeansNo goes into the Western Canadian Music Hall of Fame
years.p: They play "Now", "Going Nowhere" and "Dad" on acoustic guitar and piano, about ten minutes. Wikipedia lists a New Year's Eve Ramones set as their last show.
years.xp: Sources disagree on the induction date: Wikipedia says June 10, Punknews's John Wright interview says September 20. Byron Slack is on drums for the New Year's Eve set. John Wright on the honor: "If you just last long enough, people start to notice."

years.h: John Wright announces NoMeansNo's retirement
years.p: Tom Holliston had said he was leaving in August, and the band had gone quiet after touring through 2013.
years.xp: John Wright goes on as songwriter and musical director of Compressorhead, a robot rock band built by Berlin artist Frank Barnes. Holliston keeps playing with Showbusiness Giants and solo.

eras.title: Wrong wins one more vote
eras.text: The band is done, and its records aren't. A public vote crowns Wrong, an oral history lands and Alternative Tentacles brings the band home.

years.h: Wrong wins the Polaris Heritage Prize public vote
years.p: John Wright's answer when people call Wrong the best NoMeansNo record, in a Big Takeover interview.
years.xp: The 2021 Polaris Music Prize Heritage award is decided by a public vote among shortlisted classics. Wright says it is natural that most bands have one album they are most associated with.

years.h: PM Press publishes Jason Lamb's NoMeansNo: From Obscurity to Oblivion
years.p: The authorized oral history has a foreword by Fred Armisen. Lamb interviewed the band's members plus managers, roadies and family.
years.xp: Wikipedia dates it to December 2023; PM Press lists January 2, 2024. John Wright also starts Dead Bob in 2023; its album Life Like comes out that November.

years.h: Wrong comes home to Alternative Tentacles
years.p: The reissue is Virus #77, mastered from the original analog master by George Horn, John Wright and Jello Biafra.
years.xp: Alternative Tentacles calls it the band's return to the label. Vinyl variants include black, red, white and red-and-black split.
